source_text: perductum enim illum ad Pilatum onerare coeperunt, quod se regem diceret Christum, sine dubio (dei filium sessurum ad dei dexteram). ceterum alio eum titulo grauassent, incerti an filium se dei dixisset, (ni)si ('uos s dicitis* sic pronuntiasset, hoc se esse, quod dicerent. Pilato quoque interroganti: tu es Christus? proinde: tu dicis, ne metu potestatis uideretur amplius respondisse, (respondit.) Constitutus est igitur dominus in iudicio — et statuit in iudicio populum suum; ipse dominus in iudicium uenit cum presbyteris et archontibuspopuli, secundum Esaiam — atque exinde omne scriptum passionis suae impleuit: tumultuatae suntibidem nationes et populi meditati suntinania; adstiterunt reges terrae etarchontes congregati sunt in unum aduersus dominum et aduersus Christum eius: 'nationes' Romani qui cum Pilato fuerant; 'populi' tribus Israhelis; (reges) in Herode, (archontes) in summis sacerdotibus.
pass_a_gloss: For they began to burden him, having led him to Pilate, because he was saying that he is the Christ King, without a doubt, the Son of God who will sit at the right hand of God. However, they would have burdened him with another title, uncertain whether he had said that he is the Son of God, unless he had pronounced thus: 'You say so, this is what I am, what you say.' Also, when Pilate was questioning: 'Are you the Christ?' then: 'You say so', so that he might not seem to have responded further out of fear of power. Therefore, the Lord was placed in judgment, and he stands in judgment of his people; the Lord himself came into judgment with the elders and rulers of the people, according to Isaiah. And from then on, every scripture of his passion was fulfilled: the nations were tumultuous there, and the people meditated on vanities; the kings of the earth stood, and the rulers were gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ. The 'nations' are the Romans who were with Pilate; the 'people' are the tribes of Israel; the 'kings' are in Herod, the 'rulers' are in the high priests.

pass_b_english: They dragged him before Pilate and started loading on the charges: he claimed to be the Christ, a King—no question about it, the Son of God destined to sit at God's right hand. They would have pinned a different title on him if they weren't sure whether he'd actually called himself God's Son—unless he'd answered the way he did: 'You say so. I am exactly what you say I am.' When Pilate pressed him—'Are you the Christ?'—he gave the same line: 'You say so,' just so he wouldn't look like he was saying more out of fear of the man's authority. So the Lord takes his stand in the dock—and he stands there to judge his own people. The Lord himself walks into the courtroom alongside the elders and rulers of the people, just as Isaiah said. And from that moment every scripture of his passion clicks into place: 'The nations rage, the peoples plot empty things; the kings of the earth take their stand, the rulers gather as one against the Lord and against his Anointed' (Psalm 2:1-2). The 'nations' are the Romans standing with Pilate; the 'peoples' are the tribes of Israel; the 'kings' find their face in Herod, the 'rulers' in the high priests.
